Thanks Diego — forwarding proposed plan and role assignments from our ops side. Attaching the runbook and network checklist.

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- Maintenance window: Tue, Jul 27, 22:00-00:00 PDT (2 hours) with a 1-hour preflight starting at 21:00.
- Phased canary: 5% traffic -> 33% -> 100% over 30/45/60 minutes depending on telemetry.
- Pinning: we will pin serving nodes to 1.9.0 and only move the control plane initially to 1.9.3; full unpin after 24h stability if desired.
- Rollback: immediate rollback to 1.9.0 if: token latency P95 increases > 40% over baseline for >5 minutes OR tail error rate spikes > 0.8%.
- Network: allow TCP:443 egress to redwood-updates.redwood.ai and redwood-metrics.redwood.ai during the window (for health checks and downloads).

Operational steps (short):
1) 21:00 — Preflight: collect baseline latency/throughput (scripts in runbook), snapshot config, export KV-cache checkpoint.
2) 21:30 — Cordon 1 node from non-canary pool, drain, apply control-plane patch, run smoke tests.
3) 22:00 — Start canary slice (5%). Monitor for 15 minutes. If green, advance to 33% and re-evaluate at 30 minutes.
4) 22:45 — If metrics stable, rollout remainder gradually. If at any stage the rollback criteria hit, cut traffic and revert serving binaries to pinned 1.9.0.
5) Post window: 00:00-01:00 — Postflight, telemetry snapshot, and a reconciliation call.

Attachments referenced: redwood-private-upgrade-runbook-v2.pdf (detailed play-by-play), network-maint-checklist.xlsx (ports/ACLs).

Diego / team,

Confirmed: KV checkpoint for your on-prem setup is the same as cloud customers. Quick commands (also in runbook):
- sudo redwoodctl kv snapshot --dir=/tmp/kv-snap-$(date +%s)
- verify checksum with redwoodctl kv check --dir=/tmp/kv-snap-XXXXX

Drain note: use --drain-preserve-kv to let the node finish active KV flushes before eviction. That prevents cold-start latency post-rollout. For this micro-patch, we do not expect schema migrations.

Rollback additions:
- If rollback is triggered, set a temporary traffic-shift policy to route traffic to the dedicated 1.9.0 pool and hold for 30 minutes while we verify stability.
- If instability persists after revert, open an incident and escalate to Redwood engineering (contact on-call: engineering-oncall@redwood.com).

I'll be on the call to run the checkpoint and assist with verification.
